impact.rationale: The production delta changes the lifecycle recovery store draft-copy path immediately before preparation and publication of persistent recovery state; an error can reject recovery or construct state different from the already validated raw authority.

regressionLikelihood.rationale: The v1 marshal-error regression is source-closed by the same bound-raw fallback used for byte mismatch, and current clone-error exits remain fail closed. Coupling to a large private record graph and absent exact-candidate Go/Linux execution keep likelihood above low.

regressionProtection.rationale: Existing and added tests directly cover ordinary equivalence, byte mismatch and marshal-error raw fallback, graph detachment, representation, ownership, generation, disk and CAS boundaries, but the exact candidate has not run Go, gofmt, ordinary 688, race/full or Linux acceptance.

recoverability.rationale: The candidate is unintegrated and changes no serialized schema, migration, dependency, public API or runtime switch. A two-file revert restores the prior raw-only copy without state conversion.

confidence.rationale: The full and v1-to-v2 immutable patches, after-images and supplied receipts were hash-bound; the minimal delta, fixture reachability, signatures, clone error exits, callers, source/FMT closure and independently derived 688-name pin were inspected.

applicability.rationale: lifecycleVerifiedBase.copyRecord is called by owned internal/mihomodeploy recovery begin/revoke and candidate preparation paths; the change is a live production source path.

statusQuoRisk.rationale: The old second JSON Unmarshal remains safe and no paired exact-source Linux measurement establishes a performance benefit or quantifies the cost of keeping it.

riskDrivers: The path feeds persistent lifecycle recovery preparation and publication.
The private lifecycle graph is large and exact-candidate Go/Linux execution is intentionally absent.
No paired measurement establishes that the optimization improves the 180-second path.
protectiveFactors: The v1-to-v2 delta only changes Marshal error handling to the existing bound-raw fallback and adds one subtest.
The prior ownership, active-base, poison, raw digest, raw equality, typed equality, used-base, disk, CAS and publication gates remain unchanged.
The year-10000 fixture explicitly proves base.valid, clone success, Marshal failure, old-oracle equality, canonical/hash equality and zero writes.
Current clone error exits remain fail closed; representation cases already raw-fallback internally.
Both changed files remain in normal source/FMT closure and independently derive the unchanged 688-name SHA.
No public capability, callback, environment switch, schema, migration, dependency or history-prefix cache is introduced.

materialBoundaries.invariant: After the unchanged verified-base validity gates pass, ordinary canonical clones and all typed representation mismatches must produce the same detached record as decoding the already bound raw bytes.
materialBoundaries.counterexample: After issuance, synchronously change both store and base LastTrustedAt to UTC year 10000. b.valid remains true, clone succeeds and time.Time JSON Marshal fails, while old bound-raw JSON decoding succeeds.
materialBoundaries.legitimateControl: v2 sends either Marshal error or exact-byte inequality to lifecycleTrustedJSONCopy(b.core.raw). The fallback input is the prior validated and digest-bound raw, not caller bytes or the changed typed image.

materialBoundaries.invariant: A genuine closed-clone error must not gain authority through a broader fallback unless current source proves old bound-raw equivalence.
materialBoundaries.counterexample: A nil core, schema drift, unknown clone error or clone value mismatch attempts to continue through raw fallback.
materialBoundaries.legitimateControl: copyRecord still fails closed on clone error. nil core is excluded by b.valid; schema closure already succeeded during verifiedBase issuance and is process-stable; all current representation-error assignments invoke raw copy inside clone; no other c.err assignment exists and the closed graph excludes maps/interfaces/functions.

materialBoundaries.invariant: The optimization must not bypass ownership, active-base, poison, used-base, generation, disk custody, preparation, CAS or publication checks.
materialBoundaries.counterexample: A foreign store, spent base, changed validation generation, or disk image changed after draft copy attempts publication.
materialBoundaries.legitimateControl: b.valid/issuedTo, validated snapshot binding, disk reread, base.used, preparation and publication checks remain outside and unchanged; existing and added cases target the actual gates.

materialBoundaries.invariant: The optimized draft must not share mutable pointers, slices, bytes, aliases, spare capacity, nil/empty distinctions or RawMessage storage with store/base.
materialBoundaries.counterexample: Mutating returned ControlBytes, capabilities, sibling pointers or hidden slice capacity changes the trusted source graph.
materialBoundaries.legitimateControl: Closed clone helpers allocate each pointer/slice path and copy bytes; schema rejects maps/interfaces/functions; existing properties cover 63 structs, 86 mutable slots, aliases, nil/empty/capacity and representation fallbacks.

materialBoundaries.invariant: Both changed Go files remain in normal source/gofmt closure and added coverage must not alter the required top-level test-name set.
materialBoundaries.counterexample: A changed file is omitted from source/FMT or a new top-level test silently changes the 688-name contract.
materialBoundaries.legitimateControl: Static inspection finds both changed paths in run_contracts.sh and check_contracts.py, the test remains selected, and independent required_names extraction returns 688 with SHA b0a464294a9dcaf7bea46ea29c0e7bc4937acc63b16df05387d3652efbbcb280; all new cases are subtests.
